page: Microsoft Azure FX16-4mds_v2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz with 2 physical cores and 4 vCPUs. The hardware configuration includes an exceptionally large memory allocation of 336.0 GB, translating to 84.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance is equipped with a 945 GB NVMe SSD, while no GPUs are included. The CPU features a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX for accelerated matrix operations.

Performance benchmarks reveal a strong single-core profile but limited multi-core scaling due to the low core count. The server achieves a top-tier Geekbench single-core score of 2357.0 and strong single-threaded compression performance, with gzip compression reaching 34.85 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-core benchmarks like stress-ng multi-core and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression fall into the weak category. Memory performance is mixed; while cached small-block read bandwidth is average at 345.84 GB/sec, large-block uncached read and write speeds are weak. LLM inference performance is also constrained, with text generation on a medium 7B model rated as poor.

This server offers a highly specialized resource profile, trading raw multi-core compute power for massive memory density and fast local NVMe storage. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, it is designed for workloads that require vast memory footprints but do not scale heavily on parallel CPU threads. This makes it an appropriate fit for large in-memory databases, caching layers like Redis, and memory-intensive data processing tasks that benefit from the 336 GB RAM and 945 GB local NVMe SSD without requiring high vCPU counts.
